assumptions: Impact spreads in proportion to how much a node depends on the lost flow, measured as that flow's share of the node's inbound volume.
Inventory defers impact at the receiving node: a plant with 12 days of buffer absorbs the first 12 days of the event.
Value at risk prorates monthly flow value over the days actually exposed.
The multi-level BOM is not exploded, so component-level shortages inside a plant are not traced.
Cost of disruption assumes half the lost output is never sold (margin lost) and half ships late at 0.5% of order value per day, capped at 5%. Order economics are representative demo enrichment.

actions: Move 1 unit/month of Inspection Systems for GlobalFoundries from Austin Fab to San Jose HQ (1 over the event) — needs 49.2 hrs of 282 free, leaving 9% headroom, +1,530 km to ship.
Move 1 unit/month of Metrology for Micron Technology from Austin Fab to San Jose HQ (1 over the event) — needs 49.2 hrs of 232.8 free, leaving 7.1% headroom, -1,357 km to ship.
caveats: Allocation is greedy by value at risk, not a proven optimum.
Spare units come from free hours divided by a plant's blended hours per unit, so treat unit counts as planning-grade.
Qualification, tooling and customer approval for a plant change are not modelled; a feasible reroute here may still take weeks to authorise.
Inbound component availability at the receiving plant is not re-checked.
